shared.title: Muhos: what happens to water when forest land becomes a data-centre site?
shared.opening: Real project setting and dated official evidence; an educational reconstruction, not a finding of criminal guilt or a prediction of completed construction.
shared.default_view: Open at M0 with a schematic forest/peatland setting, project boundary and nearby Oulujoki. Show a short change animation, one water card and one wider-system connection at each step. The optional rainfall replay starts off. Persistent labels distinguish reported events, planning estimates, teaching examples and unknowns.
shared.navigation: Continue, Back, direct M0–M6 timeline selection, orbit/zoom/reset camera, replay/skip animation, optional rainfall and evidence details. No mandatory task, quiz or new planning editor. Restore complete states on jumps; never accumulate impacts on replay. At M6, the older TVE1 calculation is optional historical planning detail; it never becomes an active operating forecast.
shared.pause_handling: At M2 show the current work-pause status. Continuing to M3–M6 opens a clearly labelled conditional future, not a claim that permits exist or work may resume. Essential protective/monitoring work during the pause is distinct from further development.
shared.rainfall_rule: Rainfall arrows are qualitative route illustrations. Gross rain volume is not measured runoff, treatment overflow or water entering the river. No rain replay at M1; no winter simulation. Do not animate the whole river changing colour or fish dying.

optional_questions.question: Did Google have no permissions at all?
optional_questions.answer: The documented dispute concerns EIA sequencing and, at Muhos, a water-permit requirement for drainage. Some notifications and municipal processes existed. The October authority record and police referral do not establish a criminal conviction.

optional_questions.question: Will homes lose water?
optional_questions.answer: No household shortage is established. The 2025 river-water option describes a dedicated river intake because local waterworks and aquifer capacity are insufficient for its cooling requirement. This is not evidence of an existing residential supply cut.

optional_questions.question: Will air cooling remove the construction impacts?
optional_questions.answer: Changing heat rejection does not reverse forest removal, ditching or exposed-soil runoff. The EIA air-cooling alternative needs its own confirmed operational water budget; it must not inherit the water-cooling upper estimate.

optional_questions.question: Can we stop monitoring when development pauses?
optional_questions.answer: A pause does not automatically stop rainfall, drainage or oxidation of disturbed material. Necessary protective work and monitoring have a different purpose from continued construction.

cards.title: The project sits in a river catchment.
cards.default_scene: Schematic pre-clearance forest/peatland setting; show a 571 ha planning boundary, Oulujoki and a separate weather-reference label. Do not label all land intact forest.
cards.what_changes: Reconstruct the starting setting, before the reported clearance.
cards.why: Water pathways connect land, ditches, streams and the river.
cards.wider_implication: This setting already has hydrological connections; changing vegetation and drainage can affect water beyond the boundary.
cards.limits: The packet supplies no surveyed boundary, intact-forest classification or pre-work runoff measurement.

cards.title: About 330 hectares were reported cleared.
cards.default_scene: Remove trees within an authored area-calibrated mask; label its shape schematic. Leave ground-cover removal for the next step.
cards.what_changes: Show the company-reported clearance extent, not a guessed tree count.
cards.why: Removing canopy changes interception and vegetation water use; subsequent ground disturbance is a separate intervention.
cards.wider_implication: Area removed is a documented scope figure; the change in litres of runoff from felling alone is unquantified.
cards.limits: 330 ha is approximate and is not interchangeable with the 571 ha envelope. No canopy-only runoff coefficient is assigned.

cards.title: Ditches connect disturbed land to Oulujoki.
cards.default_scene: Reveal schematic ditches, sediment-control structures and an arrow to Oulujoki. Show the current pause note. In optional summer rain, use local-pathway cues rather than whole-river pollution.
cards.what_changes: Authority documents describe 8.9 km of proposed new ditches, largely already built, and 275 ha in VA1+VA2.
cards.why: Drainage and excavation can expose sulfide-bearing material to oxygen and create acidic, metal-bearing runoff; heavy rain and snowmelt matter.
cards.wider_implication: Water protection and monitoring remain necessary while development is paused. This is a more specific local water issue than cooling demand alone.
cards.limits: Gross rain is not discharge. Exact ditch geometry, individual stripped/compacted areas, pH, metal concentrations and pollution extent are not quantified by this packet.

cards.title: A future ground-preparation step still needs water protection.
cards.default_scene: Display Conditional future. Animate compaction only schematically on an already disturbed working patch; keep monitoring and treatment icons.
cards.what_changes: A teaching continuation after the documented pause, not a claim that all compaction has happened.
cards.why: More activity can disturb surfaces and drainage; the site-specific chemistry is not captured by a generic curve number.
cards.wider_implication: A construction pause and rainfall protection are separate processes; protective work is not automatic authorization to restart development.
cards.limits: No additional disturbed area, compaction runoff increment or construction-water quantity is invented.

cards.title: Nine halls are a proposal, not the current landscape.
cards.default_scene: Display Conditional future. Add nine schematic hall blocks following the EIA layout reference, with controlled soil/washwater handling.
cards.what_changes: Represent the proposed buildings and supporting works.
cards.why: Sealed surfaces and construction materials create water-management needs.
cards.wider_implication: The river connection remains relevant during building works; treatment and monitoring must follow an actual design.
cards.limits: Hall footprints, sealed percentage, concrete quantities, workdays and total construction water are not established; none is silently scaled from SF.

cards.title: Opening is conditional on the assessed design.
cards.default_scene: Display Conditional future. Show completed schematic buildings and generic treatment/monitoring structures; no invented tank size, approval checkmark or proven treatment efficiency.
cards.what_changes: Explain readiness for a future opening without implying it has occurred.
cards.why: A proposed water-management structure does not prove that acidity, sediment and exceptional flows are controlled.
cards.wider_implication: The programme and October authority response have different dates and roles; later assessment and permissions must determine the implementable design.
cards.limits: No commissioning water, storage capacity, release rate or compliant final design is provided.

cards.title: Air cooling is reported; final water demand is unverified.
cards.default_scene: Display Conditional future and Air cooling: reported intent. Show the TVE2 closed-loop/air-cooler schematic as an illustrative planning option, not a certified final design. An optional Historical water-cooling alternative panel shows TVE1; only that panel animates river intake and return.
cards.what_changes: Explain reported air-cooling intent and the limits of the available primary planning documents.
cards.why: The river-water option needs a separate intake/treatment solution; air cooling has a different and unquantified water budget here.
cards.wider_implication: A normalized TVE1 example splits 1,000 L of pumped cooling water into 700 L evaporation and 300 L return to the river. It does not split the whole process-plus-domestic estimate.
cards.limits: 20 million m³/year is a preliminary maximum total requirement, not chosen technology, cooling-only use or observed operation. No household shortage, river-level change, thermal plume or IT-normalized efficiency is calculated. Kaleva reports intended air cooling; this packet has no verified final design or quantified TVE2 annual water budget.
